model_annotation: The image displays two line plots comparing the training reward performance of two reinforcement learning algorithms—“Llama-On-Policy” and “Llama-LUFFY”—on “Easy” and “Hard” training sets. In the top plot, labeled “Easy Training Set,” the x-axis represents “Steps” ranging from 0 to approximately 500 with major ticks every 100 steps, and the y-axis shows “Training Rewards” from 0.0 to 0.4 with ticks at 0.1 intervals. The “Llama-On-Policy-Easy” line (teal, solid) and “Llama-LUFFY-Easy” line (red, solid) both start near 0.0, rise rapidly to around 0.3 by step 100, and then plateau with minor fluctuations near 0.35–0.4 for the remainder of training. In the bottom plot, “Hard Training Set,” the x-axis again spans 0 to 500 steps, while the y-axis ranges from 0.0 to 0.2 with 0.1 intervals. Here, “Llama-On-Policy-Hard” (teal, solid) begins near 0.0, rises slightly to ~0.02 by step 50, then drops to near 0.0 and remains flat. In contrast, “Llama-LUFFY-Hard” (brown, solid) starts near 0.0, climbs steadily to ~0.1 by step 150, and continues rising with noise to reach ~0.2 by step 500. Both plots use gridlines and legends to distinguish the lines, with no log scaling or secondary axes.
